title: Marketplace Performance Analytics
summary: KPI dashboard and marketplace analytics for e-commerce performance tracking across multiple channels.
businessProblem: The business operated across multiple marketplace channels but lacked a centralized view of performance. Decision-makers struggled to identify which channels drove revenue, where operational bottlenecks occurred, and how to allocate resources effectively.
businessQuestions: Which marketplace channels drive the highest revenue and profit margins?
How do seller performance metrics vary across different product categories?
What are the seasonal trends and patterns in marketplace sales?
Where are the operational bottlenecks affecting fulfillment and customer satisfaction?

insights.title: Channel performance varies significantly
insights.description: Different marketplace channels showed significant variation in conversion rates and average order values, with some channels driving 3x higher AOV despite lower traffic.

insights.title: Clear seasonal patterns identified
insights.description: Distinct seasonal trends were uncovered, enabling proactive inventory planning and marketing budget allocation aligned with demand cycles.

insights.title: Category-level insights drive strategy
insights.description: Product category performance analysis revealed opportunities to optimize pricing and promotional strategies for underperforming segments.

impact: Enabled data-driven decision making for marketplace strategy, helping leadership allocate resources to high-performing channels and optimize operational efficiency.

title: Customer Retention & Repurchase Analytics
summary: End-to-end retention analysis of 108K orders: censoring-safe cohort retention, RFM segmentation and repurchase timing, delivered as a live-formula Excel report with 16 insight sections.
data: 108,606 orders across 22 months (Jan 2025 - Oct 2026) -> 60,289 anonymized customer records; CRM export with fulfilled / return / pending statuses; names, phone numbers and addresses excluded.
businessProblem: The business was acquiring thousands of new customers every month, but roughly three in four never ordered again and no retention baseline existed. Stakeholders could not tell whether customer quality was improving or declining, how much revenue depended on repeat buyers, when customers typically came back, or how much revenue was locked in lapsed customers - leaving retention and win-back investment unguided.
businessQuestions: What is the repeat purchase rate, and how much revenue comes from repeat customers?
How do cohorts compare on retention when every cohort gets the same observation window?
How quickly do customers place a second order, and how concentrated is revenue among frequent buyers?
Which acquisition sources and entry products bring customers back - and which only bring one-time buyers?
How large is the lapsed-customer win-back pool, and how does a return experience affect loyalty?

insights.title: A quarter of customers drives most of the revenue
insights.description: Only 27.4% of the 60,289 customers ever ordered a second time, yet repeat customers generated 58.3% of total revenue - retention, not acquisition, is the larger revenue lever.

insights.title: The second-purchase window is 30 days
insights.description: Median time to the second order is 21 days, and 63.5% of all repeat purchases happen within 30 days (87.6% within 90). Campaigns that start after the first month address an already-cooling audience.

insights.title: Cohort quality declined while volume grew
insights.description: Measured on a fair 90-day window with mature cohorts only, retention fell from 27.5% in early 2025 to around 21% in mid-2026 while new-customer volume grew about a third. Recent cohorts were flagged immature to avoid censoring bias rather than reported as declines.

insights.title: Customers rebuy the same product
insights.description: 82.7% of second orders matched the first product, making refill-reminder and subscription-style campaigns the natural next-purchase trigger instead of cross-sell.

insights.title: One third of revenue is sleeping in lapsed customers
insights.description: 11,259 repeat customers inactive for 120+ days were holding 33.3% of total revenue, and the RFM 'At risk' segment (5,809 customers, average recency 447 days) sized a concrete win-back target list.

insights.title: Return experience correlates with higher loyalty
insights.description: Customers who experienced at least one return repurchased at 42.4% versus 26.8% for those who did not (2.25 vs 1.58 average orders) - plausibly engagement from return-resolution contact. Reported as correlation, not causation.

impact: Delivered the first retention baseline for the business: a quantified 11,259-customer win-back pool holding a third of total revenue, a 30-day post-purchase window identified as the primary retention lever, evidence that acquisition is scaling faster than customer quality, and a repeatable cohort framework - ready to guide retention campaign prioritization and acquisition budget reallocation.

dataProcessing: Single-pass pandas ETL over 108,606 rows - every aggregate derived in one read
Normalized phone -> anonymized customer ID (C000001...); raw PII never exported
Customer metrics computed on Status = Success only; returns and pending orders excluded
Order history deduplicated per customer: first/second order dates, days-to-repeat, return counts
Documented limits: 08xx vs 628xx phone formats not merged, latest cohorts immature, revenue gross per source
automation: Parameter-driven recalculation: data-end / 90-day / 120-day input cells drive every flag
Cross-validation script comparing 721 report cells against independent ETL aggregates
ETL-to-report reconciliation on row counts, revenue and segment totals - 0 formula errors
Reusable workbook: change a parameter and the whole report recalculates
analytics: Cohort analysis with fixed 90-day window plus maturity flag to avoid right-censoring bias
RFM scoring: R and M as rank-based quintiles (ties averaged), F as fixed bins 1/2/3/4/5+
Time-to-repeat distribution (median / P25 / P75) and Pareto revenue concentration
Win-back segmentation: repeat customers inactive 120+ days, sized by revenue
Return-experience impact measured with an explicit correlation-not-causation caveat
visualization: Excel Insight Report: 16 sections, KPI header, live formulas throughout
4 charts: frequency, time-to-repeat, cohort trend, new vs returning revenue
Anonymized flat tables (Customer + Orders) ready to model in Power BI

title: Marketing Performance & Profitability Analytics
summary: CAC, CPL, ROI, and LTV analysis to optimize marketing spend and improve campaign profitability.
businessProblem: Marketing spend was increasing but profitability was not keeping pace. The business needed clearer visibility into customer acquisition costs, campaign ROI, and customer lifetime value to optimize marketing investment and improve profitability.
businessQuestions: Which marketing channels deliver the lowest CAC and highest ROI?
How does customer lifetime value vary across acquisition channels?
Which campaigns are driving profitable growth versus unprofitable volume?
What is the optimal budget allocation across channels?

insights.title: Channel profitability varies significantly
insights.description: Some channels drive high volume but low profitability, while others deliver higher-quality customers with better long-term value.

insights.title: LTV:CAC ratio identifies optimal channels
insights.description: Channels with higher LTV:CAC ratios were identified as candidates for increased investment to maximize profitable growth.

insights.title: Campaign-level insights inform budget allocation
insights.description: Detailed campaign analysis revealed which promotional strategies delivered sustainable returns versus one-off spikes.

impact: Enabled marketing team to optimize budget allocation and improve campaign profitability through data-driven channel selection.

title: Return & Logistics Analytics
summary: Return rate analysis and logistics KPI tracking to improve operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.
businessProblem: High return rates were impacting profitability and customer satisfaction. The business needed to understand return patterns, identify root causes, and track logistics performance to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs.
businessQuestions: Which products have the highest return rates and why?
How do return rates vary across different customer segments?
What logistics KPIs are most correlated with customer satisfaction?
How can we reduce returns through better product descriptions or quality control?

insights.title: Return rates vary significantly by product category
insights.description: Certain product categories show return rates 3x higher than others, indicating quality issues or gaps in product descriptions.

insights.title: Delivery speed impacts return rates
insights.description: Faster delivery correlates with lower return rates, suggesting that meeting customer expectations reduces return likelihood.

insights.title: Customer feedback reveals root causes
insights.description: Integration of return reason codes with customer feedback identified actionable improvements for product listings and quality control.

impact: Enabled operations team to identify high-return product categories and implement targeted improvements to reduce return rates.

title: Credit Risk Prediction — BNSP Certification
summary: End-to-end credit risk classification following the official 9-step data science workflow for the BNSP Associate Data Scientist certification.
data: 766 rows of credit approval data (deliberately dirty, semicolon-delimited)
businessProblem: A credit analyst at Bank ABC needed to anticipate loan defaults by predicting whether prospective customers would pay their loans smoothly (LANCAR) or become delinquent (MACET), based on historical payment data. Manual assessment was slow and inconsistent, risking bad loan approvals.
businessQuestions: Can historical payment data predict whether a customer will be LANCAR or MACET?
Which features are most indicative of credit risk?
Can a model achieve accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score above 80%?

insights.title: Systematic data quality issues were identified and fixed
insights.description: Validation uncovered decimal-comma numbers read as text, inconsistent gender categories, out-of-range ages, impossible negative balances, and missing values — all corrected with documented business logic.

insights.title: Ratio features strengthened model signal
insights.description: Engineered features (installment-to-loan ratio, arrears-to-balance ratio) captured relationships that raw columns alone did not convey.

insights.title: Decision Tree outperformed Naive Bayes
insights.description: Naive Bayes failed the 80% threshold on all metrics because its feature-independence assumption conflicts with strongly correlated financial features such as loan amount, installments, and arrears.

impact: All evaluation metrics exceeded the certification requirement: accuracy ~0.92, precision ~0.83, recall ~0.90, and F1-score ~0.86 — every metric above the 80% pass threshold set by the assessment.
